chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far ibn Masroor (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: He narrated to me Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Aamir, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad al-Basri, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha', who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) say:

The generous person is close to God, close to Paradise, close to the people; and the stingy stingy person is distant from God, distant from Paradise, distant from the people. And I heard him say: Generosity is a tree in Paradise; whoever holds onto one of its branches will enter Paradise.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of generosity according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: In this tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) establishes generosity (*sakha*) as a defining characteristic of the righteous, linking spiritual closeness to God with social harmony among people. The metaphor of generosity as a 'tree in Paradise' underscores its enduring nature and the certainty of reward for those who embody it, a concept deeply rooted in Shia ethical teachings on character refinement (*akhlaq*).
